zones.label: DHT11 / DHT22
facts: Interface: single-wire digital; built-in dht module
Measures temperature and humidity
DHT11: 0 to 50 °C, ±2 °C accuracy (typical)
DHT22: −40 to 80 °C, ±0.5 °C accuracy (typical)
Pins: VCC (3.3–5 V), DATA, GND
Not waterproof; wait ≥2 s between readings
Typical price on eBay: DHT11 about $1–$2, DHT22 about $2–$4 (before shipping)
Best for: simple indoor temperature + humidity projects

zones.label: BME280
facts: Interface: I2C (up to 3.4 MHz); needs the bme280.py driver
Measures temperature, humidity, and pressure
Temperature: −40 to 85 °C, ±1 °C (typical)
Humidity: 0 to 100 %RH, ±3% (typical)
Pressure: 300 to 1100 hPa, ±1 hPa (typical)
Pins: VIN (1.8–3.6 V), GND, SCL, SDA, CSB, SDO
Typical price on eBay: about $2–$4 (before shipping)
Best for: weather stations and environmental monitoring

zones.label: DS18B20
facts: Interface: 1-Wire; onewire + ds18x20 modules
Measures temperature only
−55 to 125 °C, ±0.5 °C accuracy (typical)
Waterproof stainless-steel probe
Pins: VDD (3.0–5.5 V), DATA, GND
Many sensors share one wire (each has a unique 64-bit address)
Typical price on eBay: about $1.50–$3 for a waterproof probe (before shipping)
Best for: outdoor, aquarium, and remote sensing

zones.label: SHT40
facts: Interface: I2C (a two-wire way for chips to talk); address 0x44 on most boards
Measures temperature and humidity
Temperature: −40 to 125 °C, ±0.2 °C accuracy (typical)
Humidity: 0 to 100 %RH, ±1.8% accuracy (typical)
About 10× more accurate than a DHT11 and 5× more accurate than a BME280 for temperature
Sends a checksum with every reading, so a scrambled number becomes an error instead of a wrong answer
Barely drifts: less than 0.03 °C per year
Has a tiny built-in heater that dries off water droplets
Pins: VIN (1.08–3.6 V), GND, SCL, SDA. Power it from 3V3 OUT, never the 5 V VBUS pin
Typical price on eBay: about $1.65 (before shipping). Good sensors can also be inexpensive!
Best for: careful temperature and humidity logging where accuracy matters

quiz.question: Which sensor measures temperature, humidity, AND air pressure?
quiz.explanation: The BME280 is a 3-in-1 environmental sensor: temperature, humidity, and barometric pressure, all over I2C. The DHT sensors skip pressure, the DS18B20 measures temperature only, and the SHT40 measures temperature and humidity.

quiz.question: Which sensor is waterproof and can be placed directly in liquid?
quiz.explanation: The DS18B20 comes in a sealed stainless-steel probe, so it can measure pool, aquarium, or sous-vide temperatures. The DHT, BME280, and SHT40 are not waterproof.

quiz.question: Which sensor uses a single data wire and MicroPython's built-in dht module?
quiz.explanation: The DHT11 and DHT22 use a one-wire (single data line) protocol and are read with the built-in dht module — no extra driver file needed.

quiz.question: Which sensor lets you put many probes on one data wire, each with its own address?
quiz.explanation: Every DS18B20 has a unique 64-bit ROM address, so many of them can share the same 1-Wire bus. ds.scan() returns all the addresses it finds.

quiz.question: Which sensor is the best choice for a weather station that also tracks barometric pressure?
quiz.explanation: The BME280's pressure reading lets you track weather trends and estimate altitude, which is why it is the go-to sensor for weather-station projects.

quiz.question: Which sensor is the most accurate of the four, at about ±0.2 °C?
quiz.explanation: The SHT40 is about ten times more accurate than a DHT11 (±2 °C) and about five times more accurate than a BME280 (±1 °C). Sensirion tests each chip at the factory, and the SHT40 drifts by less than 0.03 °C per year.

quiz.question: Which sensor has a tiny built-in heater that can dry off water droplets?
quiz.explanation: If the SHT40 gets damp enough for water to form on it, you can switch its heater on for a moment to dry it out. Most hobby sensors just read 99% and stay stuck there until they dry on their own.

quiz.question: Which sensor sends a checksum with every reading, so a scrambled number turns into an error?
quiz.explanation: A checksum is a small number the sensor sends along with the data. Your program checks it, so a bad reading becomes an error message instead of a wrong temperature. The SHT40 sends one with every reading.
